```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Nguyen_2022_gepotidacin"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Nguyen_2022_gepotidacin"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1111/bcp.14996> (open access, PMC9293063)
* Supplement: Supporting Information (`bcp14996-sup-0001`), which holds the
  final population PK parameter table (Table S2) and the paediatric exposure
  figures (Figures S12 and S13).

Nguyen et al. compared a Simcyp whole-body PBPK model with a NONMEM population
PK model to select paediatric intravenous doses of gepotidacin for plague under
the FDA Animal Rule. Only the population PK model is packaged here. The PBPK
model depends on the Simcyp platform's built-in physiology and CYP3A4 / GFR
ontogeny, none of which is printed in the paper.

# Population

The population PK model was fitted to 249 adults: 140 healthy volunteers from
four phase I studies (single 1-h infusions of 200-1800 mg, a single 2-h
infusion of 1800 mg, and repeat 2-h infusions of 400-1000 mg twice daily or
1000 mg three times daily, including a Japanese cohort) and 109 patients with
acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections (ABSSSI) from the phase II
study BTZ116704 (750 or 1000 mg twice daily, or 1000 mg three times daily, for
up to 10 days). Study mean ages ranged from 26.6 to 44.7 years (Table 1). The
paper reports no weight range, sex split or race distribution for the fitted
dataset. Healthy subjects and ABSSSI patients had the same PK.

For the paediatric dose selection the authors added a maturation function on
clearance, with constants fixed from a published paracetamol model, and
simulated four weight cohorts of 100 children each, aged 0.01-19.6 years and
weighing 2.5-79 kg.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Nguyen_2022_gepotidacin")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (CL, 70 kg) | log(38.0) L/h | Table S2 |
| `lvc` (V1, 70 kg) | log(20.1) L | Table S2 |
| `lq` (Q2, 70 kg) | log(3.85) L/h | Table S2 |
| `lvp` (V2, 70 kg) | log(67.1) L | Table S2 |
| `lq2` (Q3, 70 kg) | log(48.5) L/h | Table S2 |
| `lvp2` (V3, 70 kg) | log(70.3) L | Table S2 |
| `ld1_inf1h` (D1, 1-h infusion) | log(1.06) h | Table S2 |
| `ld1_inf2h` (D1, 2-h infusion) | log(2.14) h | Table S2 |
| `e_wt_cl` | 0.75 (fixed) | Table S2 footnote; Section 2.2 |
| `e_wt_vc_q_vp_q2_vp2` | 1 (fixed) | Table S2 footnote |
| `pma_tm50` | 52.2 weeks (fixed) | Section 2.2.2 |
| `pma_hill` | 3.43 (fixed) | Section 2.2.2 |
| `etalcl` | 0.0302 (17.5 CV%) | Table S2 |
| `etalvc` | 0.3727 (67.2 CV%) | Table S2 |
| `etalq` | 0.1792 (44.3 CV%) | Table S2 |
| `etalvp` | 0.1554 (41.0 CV%) | Table S2 |
| `etalq2` | 0.0578 (24.4 CV%) | Table S2 |
| `etalvp2` | 0.0098 (9.92 CV%) | Table S2 |
| `propSd` | 0.222 | Table S2, 'Residual Error' (CV% of proportional error) |
| Three-compartment structure, IV input to central | n/a | Section 2.2 |
| `CL = 38.0 * (WT/70)^0.75`; `V1, Q2, V2, Q3, V3` linear in `WT/70` | n/a | Table S2 footnote |
| `FMAT = PMA^Hill / (TM50^Hill + PMA^Hill)` on CL, below 2 years only | n/a | Section 2.2.2 equation and text |
| `PMA (weeks) = PNA (weeks) + 40` (full-term birth) | n/a | Section 2.2.2 |

The variances are `log(1 + CV^2)`. That conversion is one of the assumptions
listed at the end of this article.

# Virtual cohorts

Original observed data are not publicly available. Three virtual cohorts are
built below.

```{r helpers}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20220202)
set.seed(20220202)

# Dose and observation records for one subject set. Every dose record carries
# rate = -2 so that rxode2 uses the model's modelled infusion duration
# dur(central); TINF selects which estimated D1 applies.
make_events <- function(subj, dose_times, tinf, obs_times) {
  doses <- tidyr::expand_grid(subj, time = dose_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 1L, amt = .data$dose_mg, rate = -2, TINF = tinf)
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(subj, time = obs_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, rate = 0, TINF = tinf)
  dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    dplyr::mutate(cmt = "central") |>
    dplyr::arrange(.data$id, .data$time, dplyr::desc(.data$evid)) |>
    dplyr::select("id", "time", "evid", "amt", "rate", "cmt", "WT", "PNA", "TINF", "cohort")
}

# Adult body weights: log-normal around 78 kg, truncated to the 49.5-117.9 kg
# range of the paper's adult simulation dataset (Section 2.2.1).
draw_adult_wt <- function(n) {
  wt <- exp(rnorm(n * 3, log(78), 0.2))
  wt <- wt[wt >= 49.5 & wt <= 117.9]
  wt[seq_len(n)]
}
```

## Adults at steady state (Section 2.2.1)

200 adults aged 18-71 years receive 1000 mg every 8 hours as a 2-hour infusion
for 10 days, which is the regimen the FDA Animal Rule supports. The dosing
interval at steady state is the last one, 216-224 h.

```{r cohort-adult-ss}
tau <- 8
n_adult <- 200
adult_subj <- tibble::tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_adult),
  WT = draw_adult_wt(n_adult),
  PNA = 12 * runif(n_adult, 18, 71),
  dose_mg = 1000,
  cohort = "Adult 1000 mg TID"
)
dose_times_ss <- seq(0, by = tau, length.out = 28)
obs_ss <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 216, by = 2), 216 + c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.1, 2.25, 2.5, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8))))
events_ss <- make_events(adult_subj, dose_times_ss, tinf = 2, obs_times = obs_ss)
```

## Adults after a single dose (Table 3)

Table 3 compares single 2-hour infusions of 400, 750, 1000 and 1800 mg and a
single 3-hour infusion of 1500 mg. Each arm has 100 adults.

```{r cohort-adult-sd}
sd_arms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~cohort, ~dose_mg, ~tinf,
  "400 mg (SD)", 400, 2,
  "750 mg (SD)", 750, 2,
  "1000 mg (SD)", 1000, 2,
  "1500 mg (SD, 3-h)", 1500, 3,
  "1800 mg (SD)", 1800, 2
)
n_sd <- 100
obs_sd <- sort(unique(c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.14, 2.5, 3, 3.1, 3.5, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 24, 36, 48, 72)))
events_sd <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(sd_arms)), function(i) {
  subj <- tibble::tibble(
    id = 1000L + (i - 1L) * n_sd + seq_len(n_sd),
    WT = draw_adult_wt(n_sd),
    PNA = 12 * runif(n_sd, 18, 55),
    dose_mg = sd_arms$dose_mg[i],
    cohort = sd_arms$cohort[i]
  )
  make_events(subj, 0, tinf = sd_arms$tinf[i], obs_times = obs_sd)
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events_sd[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

## Children (Section 2.2.2, Figures S12 and S13)

The paper built its paediatric dataset from CDC and WHO growth charts. Here
ages are drawn uniformly within each age bracket of Table 2, and weights come
from an approximate median weight-for-age curve with 12% log-normal spread.
Subjects whose weight falls outside the cohort's weight bracket are redrawn.
Every child receives 2-hour infusions every 8 hours for 10 days. Doses are
10 mg/kg for 5 kg and under (the final PopPK dose; 13 mg/kg is also
simulated), 16 mg/kg above 5 kg up to 10 kg, 19 mg/kg above 10 kg up to 40 kg,
and a fixed 1000 mg above 40 kg.

```{r cohort-paed}
# Approximate median weight-for-age (WHO under 2 years, CDC above), age in months.
wfa_age <- c(0, 1, 3, 6, 12, 24, 60, 120, 168, 216, 240)
wfa_wt <- c(3.3, 4.4, 6.1, 7.7, 9.6, 12.2, 18.3, 31.9, 50.0, 65.0, 70.0)
median_wt <- function(pna) exp(approx(wfa_age, log(wfa_wt), xout = pna, rule = 2)$y)

paed_cohorts <- tibble::tribble(
  ~cohort, ~age_lo, ~age_hi, ~wt_lo, ~wt_hi, ~mgkg, ~fixed_mg,
  "<=5 kg, 10 mg/kg", 0.12, 3, 0, 5, 10, NA,
  "<=5 kg, 13 mg/kg", 0.12, 3, 0, 5, 13, NA,
  ">5-10 kg, 16 mg/kg", 3, 12, 5, 10, 16, NA,
  ">10-40 kg, 19 mg/kg", 12, 168, 10, 40, 19, NA,
  ">40 kg, 1000 mg", 168, 235, 40, 200, NA, 1000
)
draw_paed <- function(n, age_lo, age_hi, wt_lo, wt_hi) {
  out <- tibble::tibble(PNA = numeric(0), WT = numeric(0))
  while (nrow(out) < n) {
    pna <- runif(4 * n, age_lo, age_hi)
    wt <- median_wt(pna) * exp(rnorm(4 * n, 0, 0.12))
    keep <- wt > wt_lo & wt <= wt_hi
    out <- dplyr::bind_rows(out, tibble::tibble(PNA = pna[keep], WT = wt[keep]))
  }
  out[seq_len(n), ]
}
n_paed <- 100
events_paed <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(paed_cohorts)), function(i) {
  pc <- paed_cohorts[i, ]
  subj <- draw_paed(n_paed, pc$age_lo, pc$age_hi, pc$wt_lo, pc$wt_hi) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      id = 5000L + (i - 1L) * n_paed + dplyr::row_number(),
      dose_mg = if (is.na(pc$fixed_mg)) pc$mgkg * .data$WT else pc$fixed_mg,
      cohort = pc$cohort
    )
  make_events(subj, dose_times_ss, tinf = 2, obs_times = obs_ss)
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events_paed[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Nguyen_2022_gepotidacin")
sim_ss <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events_ss, keep = "cohort")
sim_sd <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events_sd, keep = "cohort")
sim_paed <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events_paed, keep = c("cohort", "WT", "PNA"))
stopifnot(
  !anyNA(sim_ss$Cc), !anyNA(sim_sd$Cc), !anyNA(sim_paed$Cc)
)
```

# Concentration-time profiles

The adult steady-state profile below has the same regimen as the VPC panel D
of Figure S9 (1000 mg IV every 8 hours as a 2-hour infusion).

```{r profile-adult, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
sim_ss |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= 192) |>
  dplyr::group_by(time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = median(Cc), Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time - 192, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time since dose on day 9 (h)", y = "Gepotidacin (ug/mL)",
    title = "Adults, 1000 mg TID as 2-h IV infusions: median and 90% interval",
    caption = "Compare with Figure S9 panel D of Nguyen 2022."
  )
```

```{r profile-paed, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
sim_paed |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= 216) |>
  dplyr::group_by(cohort, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(Q50 = median(Cc), Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(time - 216, Q50, colour = cohort, fill = cohort)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.12, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Time since last dose (h)", y = "Gepotidacin (ug/mL)",
    colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
    title = "Children at steady state: median and 90% interval by weight cohort"
  )
```

# PKNCA validation

The paper derived its simulated exposures from concentrations that included
the residual error: "Each simulation was performed 200 times/subject in
NONMEM using parameter estimates from the validated population PK model in
adults, including the interindividual variability and residual error"
(Section 2.2.2). The comparisons below therefore run PKNCA on the simulated
observations (`sim`, which is `Cc` with the 22.2% proportional error added),
not on the individual predictions `Cc`. This matters for Cmax and not for AUC.
The largest of several noisy samples around the peak lies above the true
peak, while noise averages out over the trapezoids of an AUC. The adult
steady-state section shows both versions.

```{r nca-functions}
# conc_col = "sim" uses the simulated observations (with residual error);
# conc_col = "Cc" uses the individual predictions. The chosen column is
# renamed to Cc for PKNCA. A proportional error can, very rarely, push a
# simulated observation below zero; it is floored at zero.
run_nca <- function(sim, events, start, end, params, conc_col = "sim") {
  conc <- as.data.frame(sim) |>
    dplyr::mutate(Cc = pmax(.data[[conc_col]], 0)) |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
    dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, cohort)
  doses <- events |>
    dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
    dplyr::select(id, time, amt, cohort) |>
    as.data.frame()
  intervals <- data.frame(start = start, end = end)
  for (p in params) intervals[[p]] <- TRUE
  PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
    PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | cohort + id),
    PKNCA::PKNCAdose(doses, amt ~ time | cohort + id),
    intervals = intervals
  ))
}
```

## Adults at steady state (Table 3, last row; Section 3.2.3)

The paper's PopPK simulation reported geometric means of 8.93 ug/mL (Cmax)
and 25.3 ug*h/mL (AUC0-tau). It also reported the adult 5th and 95th
percentiles that framed the paediatric dose selection: 5.98 and 13.4 ug/mL for
Cmax, and 17.5 and 36.5 ug*h/mL for AUC0-tau.

```{r nca-ss}
wide_nca <- function(nca) {
  as.data.frame(nca) |>
    dplyr::select(cohort, id, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)
}
ss_ind <- wide_nca(run_nca(sim_ss, events_ss, 216, 224, c("cmax", "auclast")))
ss_ipred <- wide_nca(run_nca(sim_ss, events_ss, 216, 224, c("cmax", "auclast"), conc_col = "Cc"))
gm <- function(x) exp(mean(log(x)))
summ3 <- function(x) c(gm(x), quantile(x, 0.05), quantile(x, 0.95))

ss_cmp <- tibble::tibble(
  Statistic = c("Geometric mean", "5th percentile", "95th percentile"),
  cmax_pub = c(8.93, 5.98, 13.4),
  cmax_sim = summ3(ss_ind$cmax),
  cmax_ipred = summ3(ss_ipred$cmax),
  auc_pub = c(25.3, 17.5, 36.5),
  auc_sim = summ3(ss_ind$auclast),
  auc_ipred = summ3(ss_ipred$auclast)
)
ss_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Cmax published (ug/mL)" = cmax_pub,
    "Cmax simulated, with residual error (ug/mL)" = cmax_sim,
    "Cmax from IPRED (ug/mL)" = cmax_ipred,
    "AUC0-tau published (ug*h/mL)" = auc_pub,
    "AUC0-tau simulated, with residual error (ug*h/mL)" = auc_sim,
    "AUC0-tau from IPRED (ug*h/mL)" = auc_ipred
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Adults, 1000 mg TID as 2-h infusions, steady state (216-224 h).")
```

With residual error included, the simulated geometric means and the 5th and
95th percentiles match the published values. The Cmax computed from the
individual predictions is about 15% lower, which shows how much the residual
error contributes.

```{r check-ss}
pct <- function(sim, ref) 100 * (sim / ref - 1)
stopifnot(
  # A wrong clearance, volume or unit moves the geometric means by tens of
  # percent. The geometric mean is a centre, not an extreme, so it is stable
  # across rxode2 builds and thread counts.
  abs(pct(ss_cmp$cmax_sim[1], 8.93)) < 10,
  abs(pct(ss_cmp$auc_sim[1], 25.3)) < 10,
  # The 5th / 95th percentiles of 200 subjects are robust quantiles, not
  # extremes. They framed the paper's paediatric dose selection.
  all(abs(pct(ss_cmp$cmax_sim[2:3], c(5.98, 13.4))) < 15),
  all(abs(pct(ss_cmp$auc_sim[2:3], c(17.5, 36.5))) < 15),
  # The residual-error inflation of Cmax is real and AUC is unaffected.
  ss_cmp$cmax_sim[1] > ss_cmp$cmax_ipred[1] * 1.05,
  abs(pct(ss_cmp$auc_sim[1], ss_cmp$auc_ipred[1])) < 3
)
```

## Adults after a single dose (Table 3)

Table 3 reports AUC(0-t) with no stated sampling end. The simulated value is
AUC to 72 h, which is within a few percent of AUC0-inf for this model.

```{r nca-sd}
nca_sd <- run_nca(sim_sd, events_sd, 0, 72, c("cmax", "auclast"))

published_sd <- tibble::tribble(
  ~cohort, ~cmax, ~auclast,
  "400 mg (SD)", 3.02, 9.65,
  "750 mg (SD)", 5.66, 18.1,
  "1000 mg (SD)", 7.55, 24.1,
  "1500 mg (SD, 3-h)", 10.0, 37.3,
  "1800 mg (SD)", 13.6, 43.4
)

geo_sd <- as.data.frame(nca_sd) |>
  dplyr::group_by(cohort, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(geomean = exp(mean(log(PPORRES))), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = geomean)

sd_cmp <- published_sd |>
  dplyr::inner_join(geo_sd, by = "cohort", suffix = c("_pub", "_sim")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    cmax_pct = pct(cmax_sim, cmax_pub),
    auc_pct = pct(auclast_sim, auclast_pub)
  )
sd_cmp |>
  dplyr::select(cohort, cmax_pub, cmax_sim, cmax_pct, auclast_pub, auclast_sim, auc_pct) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen" = cohort,
    "Cmax published (ug/mL)" = cmax_pub,
    "Cmax simulated (ug/mL)" = cmax_sim,
    "Cmax % diff" = cmax_pct,
    "AUC published (ug*h/mL)" = auclast_pub,
    "AUC0-72 simulated (ug*h/mL)" = auclast_sim,
    "AUC % diff" = auc_pct
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Single doses: geometric means, PopPK column of Table 3 vs. this simulation.")
```

```{r check-sd}
stopifnot(
  abs(median(sd_cmp$cmax_pct)) < 10,
  abs(median(sd_cmp$auc_pct)) < 10,
  all(abs(sd_cmp$cmax_pct) < 20),
  all(abs(sd_cmp$auc_pct) < 20)
)
```

## Children at steady state (Figures S12 and S13, Table 2)

Figures S12 and S13 plot the geometric mean steady-state Cmax and AUC0-tau of
each paediatric cohort. The published values below were digitised from those
figures by the maintainers (about +/- 0.2 ug/mL and +/- 0.5 ug*h/mL). The
figures show the final PopPK doses only, so the 13 mg/kg arm for 5 kg and
under has no digitised reference. It is reported for comparison with Table 2.

```{r nca-paed}
nca_paed <- run_nca(sim_paed, events_paed, 216, 224, c("cmax", "auclast"))
paed_ind <- as.data.frame(nca_paed) |>
  dplyr::select(cohort, id, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)

published_paed <- tibble::tribble(
  ~cohort, ~cmax_pub, ~auc_pub,
  "<=5 kg, 10 mg/kg", 8.3, 26.4,
  "<=5 kg, 13 mg/kg", NA, NA,
  ">5-10 kg, 16 mg/kg", 9.8, 27.1,
  ">10-40 kg, 19 mg/kg", 10.1, 25.9,
  ">40 kg, 1000 mg", 10.9, 30.5
)

paed_cmp <- paed_ind |>
  dplyr::group_by(cohort) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    cmax_sim = exp(mean(log(cmax))),
    auc_sim = exp(mean(log(auclast))),
    cmax_lt5 = 100 * mean(cmax < 5.98),
    cmax_gt95 = 100 * mean(cmax > 13.4),
    auc_lt5 = 100 * mean(auclast < 17.5),
    auc_gt95 = 100 * mean(auclast > 36.5),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(published_paed, by = "cohort") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    cmax_pct = pct(cmax_sim, cmax_pub),
    auc_pct = pct(auc_sim, auc_pub),
    cohort = factor(cohort, levels = paed_cohorts$cohort)
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(cohort)

paed_cmp |>
  dplyr::select(cohort, cmax_pub, cmax_sim, cmax_pct, auc_pub, auc_sim, auc_pct) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Cohort" = cohort,
    "Cmax digitised (ug/mL)" = cmax_pub,
    "Cmax simulated (ug/mL)" = cmax_sim,
    "Cmax % diff" = cmax_pct,
    "AUC0-tau digitised (ug*h/mL)" = auc_pub,
    "AUC0-tau simulated (ug*h/mL)" = auc_sim,
    "AUC % diff" = auc_pct
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Children at steady state: geometric means vs. Figures S12 and S13.")
```

Table 2 (PopPK rows) gives the percentage of children whose exposure falls
outside the adult 5th-95th percentile range. Those percentages come from
80 000 simulated children (200 replicates of 400). The 100-child cohorts here
estimate them only roughly, so the table is for orientation and is not
asserted.

```{r table2}
table2 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~cohort, ~p_cmax_lt5, ~p_cmax_gt95, ~p_auc_lt5, ~p_auc_gt95,
  "<=5 kg, 10 mg/kg", 7.0, 1.0, 5.0, 8.0,
  "<=5 kg, 13 mg/kg", 0.0, 16.0, 0.0, 40,
  ">5-10 kg, 16 mg/kg", 2.0, 11, 5.0, 15,
  ">10-40 kg, 19 mg/kg", 0.0, 9.0, 3.0, 5.0,
  ">40 kg, 1000 mg", 0.0, 21, 1.0, 22
)
paed_cmp |>
  dplyr::mutate(cohort = as.character(cohort)) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(table2, by = "cohort") |>
  dplyr::select(cohort, p_cmax_lt5, cmax_lt5, p_cmax_gt95, cmax_gt95, p_auc_lt5, auc_lt5, p_auc_gt95, auc_gt95) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Cohort" = cohort,
    "Cmax <5th, Table 2 (%)" = p_cmax_lt5,
    "Cmax <5th, sim (%)" = cmax_lt5,
    "Cmax >95th, Table 2 (%)" = p_cmax_gt95,
    "Cmax >95th, sim (%)" = cmax_gt95,
    "AUC <5th, Table 2 (%)" = p_auc_lt5,
    "AUC <5th, sim (%)" = auc_lt5,
    "AUC >95th, Table 2 (%)" = p_auc_gt95,
    "AUC >95th, sim (%)" = auc_gt95
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Percentage of children outside the adult 5th-95th percentile range (adult limits from Section 3.2.3).")
```

```{r check-paed}
chk <- dplyr::filter(paed_cmp, !is.na(cmax_pub))
stopifnot(
  # Geometric means against the digitised figure values. The weight-for-age
  # curve used here is an approximation of the paper's CDC / WHO dataset, so
  # the bound is looser than for the adult checks. It still catches an error
  # in the maturation function, which moves the 5 kg and under cohort by
  # about a factor of 3.
  abs(median(chk$cmax_pct)) < 10,
  abs(median(chk$auc_pct)) < 10,
  all(abs(chk$cmax_pct) < 25),
  all(abs(chk$auc_pct) < 25)
)
```

## Typical-value checks against closed forms

These checks use the same drawn parameters on both sides, so their bounds are
tight. At steady state AUC0-tau equals dose / CL for any linear model. For a
70 kg adult receiving 1000 mg that is 1000 / 38 = 26.3 ug*h/mL. The
maturation factor at a postnatal age of 1 month is
`PMA^3.43 / (52.2^3.43 + PMA^3.43)` with PMA = 4.35 + 40 weeks, which is 0.363.

```{r check-typical}
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
typ_subj <- tibble::tibble(
  id = 1:2, WT = c(70, 4.4), PNA = c(360, 1), dose_mg = c(1000, 44),
  cohort = c("adult", "infant")
)
events_typ <- make_events(typ_subj, dose_times_ss, tinf = 2,
                          obs_times = 216 + seq(0, 8, by = 0.05))
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = events_typ, keep = "cohort",
                           atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-10)
auc_typ <- sim_typ |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(auc = sum(diff(time) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2))
fmat_1m <- (1 * 30.4375 / 7 + 40)^3.43 / (52.2^3.43 + (1 * 30.4375 / 7 + 40)^3.43)
cl_infant <- 38 * (4.4 / 70)^0.75 * fmat_1m
expected <- c(1000 / 38, 44 / cl_infant)
knitr::kable(
  tibble::tibble(
    Subject = c("70 kg adult, 1000 mg", "1-month-old 4.4 kg infant, 10 mg/kg"),
    `AUC0-tau simulated` = auc_typ$auc,
    `Dose / CL` = expected
  ),
  digits = 3
)
stopifnot(
  abs(fmat_1m - 0.363) < 0.001,
  all(abs(auc_typ$auc / expected - 1) < 0.005)
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **IIV scale.** Table S2 reports inter-individual variability as CV% without
  saying how it was computed. The variances here use `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)`.
  If the authors reported `100 * omega` instead, the variances would be
  0.0306, 0.4516, 0.1962, 0.1681, 0.0595 and 0.0098. Only the V1 term (67.2%)
  differs materially between the two readings, and it does not change the
  steady-state exposures that the paper reports. The supplement gives RSEs but
  no confidence intervals for the IIV, so the two readings cannot be told
  apart from the table.
- **Residual error.** Table S2 gives one residual term, 22.2 CV% "of
  proportional error". It is encoded as a proportional error with SD 0.222.
- **No IIV correlations** are reported, so the etas are independent.
- **Infusion duration.** NONMEM estimated D1 for the 1-h and 2-h nominal
  infusions it fitted. The model applies the matching estimate when `TINF` is
  1 or 2. For any other nominal duration (for example the 3-h infusion of
  1500 mg in Table 3) it uses `TINF` itself, because the paper estimated no D1
  for those. Dose records must carry `rate = -2`.
- **Maturation function.** The paper derives postmenstrual age from postnatal
  age in months converted to weeks, plus 40 weeks for full-term birth. Months
  are converted at 30.4375 / 7 weeks per month. The factor is applied only
  below a postnatal age of 2 years, so CL steps up by about 3% at 24 months.
  This step is in the paper's method. The paper's maturation constants come
  from a paracetamol model and were not estimated from gepotidacin data.
- **Adult weight distribution.** The paper states only the range of its adult
  simulation dataset (49.5-117.9 kg). Weights here are log-normal around 78 kg,
  truncated to that range.
- **Paediatric covariates.** The paper's dataset combined CDC growth tables
  (2-20 years) and a ModelRisk age-weight joint distribution based on WHO
  charts (0.01-12 years). Neither is available, so ages are drawn uniformly
  within each Table 2 age bracket and weights come from an approximate median
  weight-for-age curve with 12% spread, redrawn until they fall inside the
  cohort's weight bracket.
- **Exposure basis.** Simulated Cmax and AUC0-tau are computed from the
  simulated observations, including residual error, as the paper did
  (Section 2.2.2). Computed from individual predictions, Cmax is about 15%
  lower and AUC is unchanged. The size of the residual-error inflation of
  Cmax depends on how many samples fall near the peak. The paper's sampling
  grid ("sparse and dense PK sampling") is not given, so the grid here is an
  assumption.
- **Paediatric reference values** were digitised by the maintainers from
  Figures S12 and S13 of the supplement.
- **PBPK model not packaged.** The Simcyp model (Table S1) relies on the
  platform's tissue volumes, blood flows, CYP3A4 abundance and ontogeny, and
  GFR maturation, none of which is printed. Its adult exposures (PBPK column
  of Table 3) agree with the PopPK model to within about 20%.
- No erratum or correction notice for this article was found as of
  2026-10-02.
